finding: The V5 PCA sleeve predicts a next standardized idiosyncratic return, converts it into a price-like q_yes, and then routes that q_yes through terminal binary Kelly sizing and resolved-outcome Brier scoring. A short-horizon mark-to-market forecast does not identify terminal payout probability. The in-memory PCA history also stores only prices, while bootstrap and live observations arrive on different cadences, so one index step is not a stable chronological horizon.

deterministic_counterexample.interpretation: Identification counterexample only; not a live PnL estimate. The same one-step price forecast can coexist with terminal probabilities that imply either negative or positive terminal EV.

configured_horizon_mix_diagnostic.assumption: one live observation appended per configured 15-second sleep; actual loop duration is processing time plus sleep, so these are cadence approximations
configured_horizon_mix_diagnostic.interpretation: Adjacent price differences from radically different elapsed times are treated as exchangeable one-step returns because timestamps are not retained in the PCA in-memory history. The estimation target therefore changes with runtime age unless history is explicitly time-aligned/resampled.

distinct_from_existing_research: #174 timestamp alignment of V5 PCA history; prerequisite and partially related to making chronological horizons explicit
required_common_sample_experiment: timestamp-align/resample the PCA panel first so the target horizon is explicitly chronological rather than an observation index
evaluate PCA as an explicit mark-to-market model at fixed future horizons such as 15m, 30m, 1h and 6h using purged chronological event/time-clustered rows
compare bounded cost-aware markout sizing against the incumbent terminal-binary Kelly interpretation
if PCA state is used for terminal probability, fit a separate time-to-resolution calibration/decoder only on prior resolved events and report Brier, log-loss and calibration error
compare incumbent and separated-semantics variants on identical rows with executable OOS PnL, turnover, capital occupancy and drawdown at 1x, 1.5x and 2x costs
control the timestamp, residual-inference and singleton-confidence defects jointly before attributing incremental utility to the horizon-semantics change
